title: Brandin Podziemski back in Warriors' starting lineup for game vs. Grizzlies

 Marcus D. Smith USA TODAY Updated Oct. 23, 2026, 10:45 p.m. ET Hear this story SAN FRANCISCO — Golden State Warriors guard Brandin Podziemski started in the team's home opener against the Memphis Grizzlies on Friday, Oct. 23.
 But his initial appearance proved to be brief. Podziemski left the game with 8:17 left in the first quarter after taking a shot from Grizzlies center Zach Edey.
 Podziemski went backdoor and took a pass from Graham Ike as he went up for a layup over Edey. Podziemski scored but not without contact. Edey appeared to have struck Podziemski in the face as he was making a play on the ball. No whistle was blown and everyone played on ... except Podziemski, who stayed on the ground after the contact.
 He got up and walked off the court and into the locker room on his own. Podziemski had scored four points, making both shot attempts.
 He did eventually return to the bench and get back into the game.
 All things Warriors: Latest Golden State Warriors news, schedule, roster, stats, injury updates and more. Podziemski missed the Warriors' season opener, Wednesday's 127-105 loss to the Los Angeles Lakers, due to a sore back.
 Warriors head coach Steve Kerr told reporters before Friday's game that Podziemski was not only available, but starting at the two-guard position.
 "He had a workout this morning," Kerr said. "Went through it fine, so he'll be in the starting lineup."
 Podziemski appeared in all 82 games for the Warriors last season. His availability was one of the many attributes that gave Golden State confidence before extending the 23-year-old.
 The Warriors and Podziemski agreed to a five-year, $110 million rookie-scale contract extension, which includes an option for the final year in 2031–32.
 Podziemski averaged career highs with Golden State last year (13.8 points per game, 3.7 assists, 1.1 steals on 45% shooting). The Warriors drafted Podziemski out of Santa Clara with the 19th overall pick in the 2023 NBA Draft.
